scenes.title: A Look Around India
narration: Have you noticed the beautiful peacock dancing in the park?
India has special symbols that make our country unique.
Do you know why we chose these specific ones?

scenes.title: Learning Our National Icons
narration: Our national flower is the lovely pink lotus.
The Bengal Tiger is our strong national animal.
The majestic Banyan tree is our national tree.
These represent the nature of our vast land.

scenes.title: The Mango and The River
narration: Think of a yummy, sweet yellow mango in summer.
It is our favorite fruit from the orchard.
Then there is the long and holy River Ganga.
It flows from the Himalayas to the sea.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Symbols
narration: We have symbols for our birds, trees, and rivers.
These help us remember the beauty of India.
Think about it: which national symbol is your favorite?

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever bought a yummy samosa at the school canteen?
You give the shopkeeper a coin or a paper note.
Do you know what that money is actually called?

scenes.title: What is Currency
narration: In India, our money is called the Indian Rupee.
We use coins made of metal for smaller amounts.
We use paper notes for larger amounts of money.
The symbol for the rupee looks like this.

scenes.title: Example of Buying
narration: Imagine you want to buy a pencil for five rupees.
You can give one five-rupee coin to the seller.
Or you could give five one-rupee coins.
Both add up to the same total value.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Indian money is called the rupee and comes in coins and notes.
We use it to trade for things we need or want.
Think about it: Why do you think money is better than trading toys?

scenes.title: The Big Map of India
narration: Have you ever looked at a big map of India in your classroom?
India has many states, and each state has its own special home city.
These main cities are called capital cities. Do you know why they are important?

scenes.title: What Makes a Capital?
narration: A capital city is where the government works to help the people.
It is like the heart of the state where big decisions are made.
Every state in India has one capital city to lead the way.

scenes.title: Seeing Capitals in Action
narration: Think of Maharashtra, a big state. Mumbai is its busy capital city.
Think of Karnataka. Bengaluru is its capital, famous for many trees.
New Delhi is our national capital, where the whole country comes together.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Capitals are important cities where leaders work for their states.
India has many states, and each one has its own special capital.
Can you find out the name of the capital city of your own state?

scenes.title: Have you seen big cities?
narration: Have you ever traveled to a place with tall buildings and many cars?
India has many big cities, each with its own special story.
Let us learn about some famous cities in our country today!

scenes.title: Discovering Major Cities
narration: New Delhi is our capital city with the beautiful India Gate.
Mumbai is a busy city near the sea, famous for big movies.
Kolkata is known for its grand bridges and yummy sweets.
Chennai is a sunny city in the south near the beach.

scenes.title: A Look at New Delhi
narration: Imagine we are visiting New Delhi right now.
We see the wide roads and the flag flying high.
The government works here to help all of India.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: India has many cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai.
Every city is different and full of life.
Which big city would you like to visit one day?

scenes.title: A World of Wonders
narration: Have you ever seen a building that looks like a giant white marble palace?
India is full of amazing places that tell stories from long ago.
Let us travel across India to find some very special spots.

scenes.title: Learning About Landmarks
narration: First, we go to Agra to see the beautiful Taj Mahal.
It is made of shiny white marble that glows under the moon.
Next, we visit Delhi to see the tall Qutub Minar.
It is a very old and very tall stone tower.

scenes.title: Seeing More Gems
narration: Now we go to Jaipur to see the Hawa Mahal.
It is a pink palace with hundreds of tiny windows.
Finally, we visit the Gateway of India in Mumbai.
It stands right by the big blue sea.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Travels
narration: We saw the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, Hawa Mahal, and Gateway of India.
These places help us remember the rich history of India.
Which of these famous places would you like to visit first?

scenes.title: Who was Nehru?
narration: Have you seen a rose pinned to a person's jacket in old photos?
That is Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, our country's first Prime Minister.
He was a very important leader who helped India become free.

scenes.title: A Friend to Children
narration: Pandit Nehru loved children very much and called them the future.
He felt children were like little buds in a garden.
Because he loved kids, we celebrate his birthday as Children's Day.
Every year on November 14th, we remember his big smile.

scenes.title: Working for India
narration: He worked hard to build schools and big factories in India.
He wanted every child in India to go to school.
He also helped create big dams to give water to farmers.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Leader
narration: Pandit Nehru was a brave leader who loved India dearly.
We remember him today for his kindness and his work.
Think about it: Why do you think he loved children so much?

scenes.title: Meet the Rare Animals
narration: Have you seen a tiger at the zoo or in a picture book?
Some animals are becoming very rare and hard to find.
We call these endangered animals because they need our help.

scenes.title: Why They Need Help
narration: Animals need forests to live, eat, and play safely.
Sometimes, people cut down too many trees for buildings.
When homes disappear, animals have nowhere left to go.
Pollution also makes it very hard for them to stay healthy.

scenes.title: The Great Indian Rhino
narration: Let us look at the One-Horned Rhino in Assam.
They love to splash in the grassy wetlands.
In the past, their homes were taken away by people.
Now, parks protect them so they can grow their families.

scenes.title: How You Can Help
narration: We can protect animals by keeping our forests green.
Always remember to keep our environment clean and plastic-free.
Think about it: what is one way you can help animals today?

scenes.title: A Great Indian Hero
narration: Have you ever looked at a rocket zoom into the sky?
A special man named APJ Abdul Kalam helped build these rockets.
He was a very famous scientist from India.

scenes.title: Learning and Working Hard
narration: Abdul Kalam was born in Rameswaram by the sea.
As a boy, he worked hard to deliver newspapers.
He loved books and studying about science.
He worked for many years to help India build technology.

scenes.title: The People's President
narration: In 2002, he became the 11th President of India.
He loved talking to students in schools.
He told children to dream big and work hard.

scenes.title: Remembering His Great Lessons
narration: Abdul Kalam taught us to be brave and kind.
He is remembered as the Missile Man of India.
Think about it: what is one big dream you have for your future?

scenes.title: A Hero For India
narration: Have you seen a statue of a brave man in a military uniform?
That is Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, a great freedom fighter.
He wanted India to be free from British rule.

scenes.title: Leading The Way
narration: Netaji was born in Cuttack, Odisha, in the year 1897.
He believed that India needed a strong army to get freedom.
He formed the Azad Hind Fauj to fight for our country.

scenes.title: His Powerful Words
narration: Netaji loved his country very much and worked very hard.
He gave us a famous slogan: Give me blood, and I will give you freedom.
This encouraged thousands of Indians to join the struggle.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Hero
narration: Netaji reminds us that we must always love and protect India.
We celebrate his birthday on January 23rd every year.
Think about it: What is one brave thing you can do for your school?

scenes.title: The Courageous Queen
narration: Have you ever seen a statue of a queen on a horse?
This is Rani Lakshmibai, a famous hero from our history.
She lived in the city of Jhansi a long time ago.

scenes.title: A Life of Bravery
narration: As a girl, she learned to ride horses and use swords.
She was very strong and loved her people very much.
She became the queen and ruled Jhansi with kindness.
She worked hard to protect her home from invaders.

scenes.title: Fighting for Freedom
narration: In 1857, she fought bravely against the British army.
She led her soldiers into the field with great courage.
Even when things were hard, she never gave up.

scenes.title: A Shining Legacy
narration: We remember her today as a symbol of Indian bravery.
Her story teaches us to be strong and stand for what is right.
Think about it: what is one way you can be brave today?

Animals and Birds: Interesting Animal Fa.topic: Animals and Birds: Interesting Animal Facts
Animals and Birds: Interesting Animal Fa.title: Amazing Animal Wonders

scenes.title: Do Animals Have Superpowers
narration: Have you ever wondered why your pet dog has such a wet nose?
Animals have amazing senses that help them live in the wild.
Let us explore how animals see, hear, and move differently.

scenes.title: How Animals See and Hear
narration: Owls are like night hunters with super big eyes for darkness.
Elephants use their giant ears to hear sounds from far away.
Cats have special whiskers to feel their way in the dark.

scenes.title: The Cheetah's Fast Run
narration: Look at the cheetah, the fastest land animal in the world.
It uses its long tail to balance while making sharp turns.
Strong claws act like running shoes to grip the ground tight.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Animals use senses and body parts to survive and move.
From big ears to fast legs, every animal is special.
If you could have one animal superpower, what would it be?

Animals and Birds: National Animals of C.topic: Animals and Birds: National Animals of Countries
Animals and Birds: National Animals of C.title: Meet The World's National Animals

scenes.title: Animals Around The World
narration: Have you seen our beautiful national animal, the Royal Bengal Tiger?
Many countries choose special animals to represent them.
Do you wonder which animal represents other countries far away?

scenes.title: Why Pick An Animal
narration: Countries pick animals that show strength or are found in their lands.
The tiger is strong and bold, just like our great country India.
Some animals are famous because they live only in that place.

scenes.title: Animals From Other Lands
narration: In the United States, the Bald Eagle flies high in the sky.
Australia loves the Kangaroo because it always moves forward.
Japan respects the Green Pheasant, a bird with beautiful, bright feathers.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned that national animals make countries feel proud and special.
Each animal tells a story about the land it calls home.
If you could pick any animal to represent your school, which one would it be?

scenes.title: The Body's Magic Parts
narration: Have you ever wondered how you run, jump, and play all day long?
Your body is like a super machine made of many clever parts.
Today, let us look at the amazing things happening inside you.

scenes.title: Bones and Muscles Work
narration: Your bones are the strong frame that keeps you standing tall.
Muscles are like stretchy bands that pull your bones to move.
Together, bones and muscles help you kick a ball or wave hello.

scenes.title: The Boss and The Pump
narration: Your brain is the boss that tells your body what to do.
Your heart is a strong pump that sends blood everywhere.
Imagine your heart beating like a drum during a game of tag.

scenes.title: Stay Healthy and Strong
narration: Eat healthy food like dal, roti, and fruits to grow strong.
Your body needs rest, water, and exercise every single day.
Think about it: which part of your body helps you smell a flower?

scenes.title: Where Do Animals Stay
narration: Have you ever wondered where your pet dog or a wild tiger sleeps at night?
Just like you have a house, every animal needs a special place to live.
This special home is called a habitat.

scenes.title: Different Types Of Homes
narration: Some animals live in forests where there are many tall trees.
Others live in the water like rivers, lakes, or the big blue ocean.
Some even live in dry, hot deserts or very cold snowy mountains.

scenes.title: Example: The Bengal Tiger
narration: Let us look at the Royal Bengal Tiger of India.
It loves living in the thick mangrove forests of the Sundarbans.
The forest gives the tiger food, water, and shade to rest.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: A habitat gives animals food, water, and a safe place to stay.
Animals are perfectly suited to live in their own homes.
Think about it: could a fish live happily in a dry desert?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Have you ever wondered how we know the world around us?
We use our five amazing senses every single day.
These senses act like messengers to our brain.

scenes.title: Using Our Senses
narration: Our eyes help us see bright colors and shapes.
Our ears listen to sounds like birds chirping.
Our nose smells sweet flowers in the garden.
Our tongue tastes yummy snacks like spicy chaat.
Our skin helps us feel if things are soft.

scenes.title: A Day at the Park
narration: Imagine we are eating a juicy mango in a park.
We see the yellow color and smell the sweet scent.
We feel the smooth skin and taste the sweet juice.
We hear the park breeze rustling the leaves nearby.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: We see, hear, smell, taste, and touch.
These senses help us explore everything we do.
Think about it, which sense do you use the most?

scenes.title: Is Air Actually Real
narration: Have you ever wondered what is inside your empty water bottle?
It is not really empty because air is hiding inside it.
We cannot see air, but we can feel it move around us.

scenes.title: What Makes Up Air
narration: Air is a mix of different invisible gases.
Plants and humans need air to stay alive.
Oxygen is the part of air that we breathe in.
Air also takes up space and has weight.

scenes.title: Air In Daily Life
narration: When you blow up a balloon, you are filling it with air.
Moving air is called wind, like a breeze in a park.
Air helps kites fly high in the blue sky.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Air
narration: Air is all around us even if we cannot see it.
It is essential for every living thing on Earth.
Think about it: how would you feel if you could see the air?

scenes.title: Looking at the Night Sky
narration: Have you ever looked at the night sky and wondered what all those twinkling lights are?
The bright ball in the center is our Sun.
Everything moving around the Sun is called our solar system.

scenes.title: The Planets and the Sun
narration: The Sun is a giant, glowing star made of hot gas.
There are eight planets that travel around the Sun in a path.
Each planet has its own special size and color.

scenes.title: Living on Planet Earth
narration: Earth is our home, the third planet from the Sun.
It is the only planet we know that has life, like plants and animals.
Earth spins around like a top, giving us day and night.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The Sun is the center, and eight planets orbit around it.
Earth is our beautiful home in this big space neighborhood.
Think about it: if you could visit another planet, which one would you choose?

scenes.title: Water in Our Daily Life
narration: Have you ever wondered where your glass of water comes from?
Or where the puddle on the road goes after it rains?
Today, we will learn about the magical water cycle!

scenes.title: How Water Moves
narration: First, the sun warms up water in our rivers and lakes.
The water turns into invisible steam and rises up high.
Up there, it cools down and turns into fluffy clouds.
When clouds get heavy, water falls back as rain or snow.

scenes.title: Following the Rain
narration: Imagine rain falling on a green mountain in India.
The water flows down into a sparkling blue river.
Finally, the river carries that water all the way to the sea.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Water rises, turns into clouds, and falls as rain.
This cycle keeps our plants, animals, and us healthy.
Think about it: how can you save water at home today?

scenes.title: The Magic of Light
narration: Have you ever wondered why you can see your toys when the sun is up?
It is because light travels from a source and hits the things around us.
Without light, our world would be pitch black, even if our eyes were open!

scenes.title: How Light Works
narration: Light acts like a messenger that carries pictures to our eyes.
The sun is our biggest light source, but we also use bulbs at home.
Light travels in a straight line, which we call a light ray.
When light hits an object, it bounces off and zooms into our eyes.

scenes.title: Seeing a Red Apple
narration: Let us look at a shiny red apple on your kitchen table.
Sunlight hits the apple and all colors get soaked up, except for red.
The red light bounces off the apple skin and lands right in your eyes.
Your brain then tells you that the apple is round and bright red.

scenes.title: Light Recap
narration: Light comes from sources like the sun and bounces off everything we see.
Our eyes catch these light rays to help us see the world clearly.
Think about it: what happens when you turn off all the lights at night?

scenes.title: The World Is Noisy
narration: Have you ever wondered how the chirping bird reaches your ears?
Sounds are everywhere, from school bells to your friend laughing.
But how does that sound actually travel to you?

scenes.title: The Secret Of Vibrations
narration: Sound is made when something moves back and forth very fast.
This back and forth movement is called a vibration.
Think of it like a wiggle that travels through the air.
These invisible wiggles bump into each other like a line of dominoes.

scenes.title: A Musical Example
narration: Imagine you are plucking a string on a Sitar in your music room.
The string vibrates quickly and pushes the air around it.
The air carries the wiggle until it reaches your ear.

scenes.title: Sound Recap
narration: Sound starts with a vibration moving back and forth.
It travels through the air to reach our ears.
Think about it: can you feel your throat vibrate when you hum a song?

scenes.title: Do you love playing games
narration: Have you ever played cricket or badminton at school?
Many people in India love sports very much.
Do you know who our famous sports heroes are?

scenes.title: Learning about our champions
narration: A champion is someone who practices very hard.
They play games to represent our country, India.
These players show us that we can be anything.

scenes.title: Meeting two Indian legends
narration: Sachin Tendulkar is a famous cricket legend.
He hit many runs for India with his bat.
P.V. Sindhu is a star at playing badminton.
She moves very fast to win medals.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: India has many great sports stars.
They practice hard to make us proud.
Which sport do you want to play today?

scenes.title: The Big Game Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered why we use different things for different sports?
At the park, you see kids using bats, balls, and even rackets.
Each game needs special tools to help us play our very best.

scenes.title: How Tools Help Us
narration: Some tools help us hit a ball far away, like a cricket bat.
Some help us move quickly and safely, like our sturdy sports shoes.
Others protect our bodies, like the helmets used in cycling.
Using the right gear makes every game more fun and safe.

scenes.title: Example: Playing Cricket
narration: Let us look at a game of cricket in the school field.
The batter holds a wooden bat to hit the hard ball.
The wicketkeeper wears big gloves to catch the ball safely.
Both players use their gear to play fairly and well.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Remember, we use different gear for different sports to play well.
Equipment also keeps us safe while we are running and playing.
Think about it: What gear would you need to play your favorite game?

scenes.title: What Do You Like Playing?
narration: Do you love running fast or hitting a ball in the park?
Sports are games that keep our bodies strong and healthy.
Let us explore some famous sports played right here in India.

scenes.title: Learning About Famous Sports
narration: Cricket is a favorite game where players use a bat and ball.
Football is played by kicking a ball into a big net goal.
Badminton uses a light racket to hit a shuttlecock over a net.
Kabaddi is an exciting traditional game from our own country.

scenes.title: Let's Play Cricket Together
narration: First, the bowler runs up and throws the ball towards the stumps.
The batsman uses the wooden bat to hit the ball far away.
Then, the batsman runs between the wickets to score many runs.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: We learned that sports keep us fit and happy every day.
Cricket, football, and kabaddi are popular games in India.
Which sport do you want to play with your friends today?

scenes.title: Watching Sports Together
narration: Do you love watching games on TV with your family?
Sometimes, the whole world watches the same big match!
These are called major sports events.

scenes.title: What Makes Them Special
narration: The Olympic Games happen every four years.
Athletes from many different countries come to compete.
They try their best to win a shiny gold medal.

scenes.title: Cricket World Cup
narration: In India, the Cricket World Cup is very popular.
Teams play hard to score many runs.
The team with the most runs wins the big trophy.

scenes.title: Remembering the Fun
narration: Big games bring the world together in peace.
Athletes practice every day to do their very best.
Which sport would you like to play in a big event?

scenes.title: The Big Blue Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered how much of our Earth is covered in water?
Look at a globe; it is mostly blue!
That blue part is made of giant oceans.

scenes.title: What Are Oceans
narration: An ocean is a huge body of very salty water.
There are five big oceans on our planet.
They hold almost all the water on Earth.
They connect all the different countries together.

scenes.title: Meet The Indian Ocean
narration: India has its very own ocean right to the south.
It is named the Indian Ocean.
Many fish and sea turtles live in its warm waters.
Large ships travel across it to bring us goods.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Oceans are giant, salty, and cover most of Earth.
We must keep our oceans clean for the animals.
Think about it: can you name one animal that lives in the ocean?

scenes.title: The Big Wide World
narration: Look at a globe or a map in your classroom.
Did you know that all the land is divided into seven giant pieces?
These giant pieces of land are called continents.

scenes.title: Learning The Seven Continents
narration: Asia is the biggest one where we live in India.
Africa is famous for wild lions and vast deserts.
North America and South America are two separate, beautiful continents.
Antarctica is the very cold continent at the bottom of the globe.
Europe and Australia are the final two to complete our set.

scenes.title: A Trip Around India
narration: Imagine you are in India, which is part of Asia.
If you flew a plane west, you would reach Europe.
If you flew a plane far south, you would reach cold Antarctica.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Remember, there are seven continents on our planet.
They are huge landmasses surrounded by deep blue oceans.
Think about it: which continent would you like to visit first?

scenes.title: What is a mountain?
narration: Have you ever climbed a very tall hill that touches the clouds?
A mountain is a huge piece of land that reaches high up.
They are much taller and steeper than the hills near your home.

scenes.title: The Mighty Himalayas
narration: In the north of India, we have the great Himalayan mountains.
These mountains are covered in thick, white snow all year long.
The air gets very cold the higher up you climb.
Many big rivers like the Ganga start from these snowy peaks.

scenes.title: Life in the Mountains
narration: People living in mountains build houses on the slopes.
They wear warm woolen sweaters and jackets to stay cozy.
Animals like the furry yak live comfortably in these cold mountains.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Mountains are super tall landforms that are often covered in snow.
They are the source of our fresh water rivers in India.
Think about it, would you like to build a house on a mountain?

scenes.title: Why Do People Dance
narration: Have you ever danced at a wedding or a school party?
In India, we have many special dances for festivals.
Do you know why we dance for these celebrations?

scenes.title: Learning Traditional Steps
narration: Traditional dances tell stories about our history and nature.
Dancers wear bright clothes and shiny jewelry.
Music with drums and bells keeps the rhythm.
Every move has a meaning, like showing a flower.

scenes.title: The Bhangra Example
narration: Let us look at Bhangra from Punjab.
Farmers dance it to celebrate the harvest season.
They jump high and wave their arms up.
The dhol drum makes everyone want to dance.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Culture
narration: India has many dances like Garba, Kathak, and Bihu.
These dances bring families and friends together happily.
Think about it, what is your favorite way to move to music?

scenes.title: The Sandy Mystery
narration: Have you ever seen a place with almost no plants and lots of sand?
That dry and sandy place is called a desert.
Why is it so dry there? Let us find out!

scenes.title: Why Deserts Are Dry
narration: Deserts are places that get very little rain all year long.
Without rain, the ground becomes very dry and dusty.
Because there is no water, only special plants can grow here.

scenes.title: Life in the Thar
narration: In India, we have the Thar Desert in Rajasthan.
Camels live here because they can walk on sand without sinking.
Cactus plants store water inside them to stay alive.

scenes.title: Remembering the Desert
narration: Deserts are dry places with very little rain and special plants.
The Thar Desert is our very own sandy home in India.
Think about it: how would you stay cool in the hot desert sun?

scenes.title: Music Is Everywhere
narration: Have you ever tapped your feet to a catchy song?
Music is a special way we share our feelings.
Do you know how Indian music started long ago?

scenes.title: Two Main Styles
narration: In the north, we have Hindustani music.
It uses instruments like the sitar and tabla.
In the south, we have Carnatic music.
It often focuses on beautiful singing called ragas.

scenes.title: Instruments in Action
narration: Let us look at a sitar with its long neck.
Next, the tabla drums make a steady beat.
Finally, the flute makes a soft, airy sound.
Together, these create a wonderful, happy song.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: India has many musical styles and instruments.
Music helps us celebrate our culture together.
Think about it: what is your favorite musical instrument?

scenes.title: Many Languages In India
narration: Have you heard your friends speak different languages at school?
India is a big country with many different ways to talk.
Why do people speak so many different languages?

scenes.title: Learning New Words
narration: Languages are like tools we use to share our feelings.
Some people speak Hindi, while others speak Bengali or Tamil.
Each language has its own special sounds and words.
It is like having a secret code for every state.

scenes.title: Examples Of Greetings
narration: In Hindi, we say Namaste to greet our elders.
In Punjabi, we say Sat Sri Akal to say hello.
In Marathi, we say Namaskar when we meet friends.
All these words mean we are being kind to others.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: India has many languages that make our country special.
Learning a new word is a way to make new friends.
Which language do you want to learn to say hello in?

scenes.title: Why do we celebrate?
narration: Have you noticed how we wear new clothes and share sweets during festivals?
India is a land of many colors and celebrations.
Do you know why we celebrate these special days together?

scenes.title: Light and Colors
narration: Diwali is the festival of lights where we light small clay lamps.
Holi is the festival of colors where we play with bright powders.
These festivals bring families and friends closer in joy.

scenes.title: Harvest and Joy
narration: In Punjab, farmers celebrate Baisakhi when the wheat is ready.
They dance with drums to say thank you for the food.
Pongal in Tamil Nadu is another harvest festival with yummy rice.

scenes.title: Celebrating Together
narration: Festivals teach us to share, care, and love one another.
All these festivals make our country beautiful and unique.
Think about it: What is your favorite festival and why do you love it?

scenes.title: Where Rivers Begin
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in a river comes from?
High up in the mountains, the snow melts into tiny streams.
These tiny streams join together to form a big, flowing river.

scenes.title: The Journey Downstream
narration: The river travels a long way down the mountain slopes.
It passes through green forests and wide, flat fields.
Farmers use this fresh river water to grow their tasty crops.

scenes.title: Example: River Ganga
narration: Let us look at the holy River Ganga in India.
It starts in the snowy Himalayas at a place called Gangotri.
It flows across plains and finally reaches the deep blue sea.

scenes.title: Rivers Are Amazing
narration: Rivers start as melted snow and flow all the way to the sea.
They give water to people, animals, and all the thirsty plants.
Think about it: what would happen if our rivers stopped flowing?

Important Days: National and Internation.topic: Important Days: National and International Days
Important Days: National and Internation.title: Why Do We Celebrate Days?

scenes.title: A Day to Remember
narration: Have you ever noticed your birthday is a very special day for you?
Did you know that our country and the world also have special birthdays?
Why do we pick specific days to celebrate things like books or trees?

scenes.title: Learning the Why
narration: Some days help us learn about our country's important history.
Other days remind us to take care of our beautiful Earth.
We celebrate these days to make sure we never forget what matters.

scenes.title: Special Days in India
narration: In India, we celebrate Independence Day on August 15th every year.
We also celebrate Republic Day on January 26th to honor our laws.
Children's Day is on November 14th to celebrate all the kids in India.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Special days teach us about our history and how to help the world.
Celebrating together makes us proud of who we are.
Think about it: which special day would you like to invent for your school?

Festivals and Culture: Traditional Cloth.topic: Festivals and Culture: Traditional Clothes and Food
Festivals and Culture: Traditional Cloth.title: Celebrating India's Colorful Traditions

scenes.title: What do we wear today?
narration: Have you ever wondered why we wear special clothes during festivals like Diwali or Eid?
In India, every state has its own beautiful traditional outfit.
These clothes tell us about our history and where our families come from.

scenes.title: Exploring Different Traditional Styles
narration: Many people in Punjab wear colourful bright turbans and comfy kurta-pyjamas.
In West Bengal, women often wear elegant sarees with a special red border.
South Indian festivals often feature crisp white mundus with golden borders.

scenes.title: Delicious Foods and Feasts
narration: Festivals are never complete without yummy traditional treats to eat together.
During Ganesh Chaturthi, we make sweet modaks that are steamed and delicious.
For Pongal in Tamil Nadu, people cook a special sweet rice dish in pots.

scenes.title: Let's Remember Our Traditions
narration: We wear traditional clothes to honor our culture and show our happiness.
Sharing special food with friends and family makes every celebration better.
Think about it: What is your favorite traditional outfit to wear at home?

Important Days: Why We Celebrate Them.topic: Important Days: Why We Celebrate Them
Important Days: Why We Celebrate Them.title: Why Do We Have Holidays?

scenes.title: The Big Red Date
narration: Have you ever seen a red date on your school calendar?
It is a special day when school is closed for everyone.
Why do we stop our work to celebrate these days?

scenes.title: Remembering Our Heroes
narration: Some days celebrate amazing people who helped build our country.
On Independence Day, we remember how India became free in 1947.
Learning their stories teaches us how to be brave and kind.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Culture
narration: Other days are for festivals that bring our families together.
Like Diwali, where we light diyas to celebrate light winning over darkness.
These days help us share love and delicious food with neighbors.

scenes.title: A Day To Remember
narration: Special days help us remember history and celebrate our shared traditions.
They remind us who we are and keep our stories alive.
If you could pick one new day to celebrate, what would it be?

scenes.title: One Big Country
narration: India is a very big country with many parts.
Each part has its own name, people and language.
What do we call these parts?

scenes.title: States and Union Territories
narration: India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories.
A state has its own government and Chief Minister.
Union Territories are looked after mostly by the central government.
Delhi, the capital of India, is a Union Territory.

scenes.title: Big and Small
narration: Rajasthan is the biggest state by size.
Goa is the smallest state by size.
Andhra Pradesh is famous for its long coastline.

scenes.title: Let Us Remember
narration: 28 states and 8 Union Territories make one India.
Every state is special in its own way.
Think about it: which state do you live in?

scenes.title: A Man in a Simple Dhoti
narration: Have you seen a picture of a smiling man with round glasses on our rupee notes?
He is Mahatma Gandhi, whom we lovingly call Bapu.
Why do we call him the Father of the Nation?

scenes.title: Truth and Non-violence
narration: Gandhiji was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
He believed in always telling the truth.
He taught us to fight without hurting anyone. This is called non-violence.

scenes.title: The Salt March
narration: In 1930, Gandhiji walked about 390 kilometres to the sea at Dandi.
He made salt from sea water to protest an unfair British law.
Millions of Indians joined him to win freedom for India.

scenes.title: Remembering Bapu
narration: We celebrate Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October every year.
He spun his own cloth on a charkha to show self-reliance.
Think about it: how can you be truthful and kind today?

Famous People: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.topic: Famous People: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
Famous People: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.title: Babasaheb Ambedkar

scenes.title: The Rule Book of India
narration: Every country needs rules so everyone is treated fairly.
India's big rule book is called the Constitution.
Do you know who led the team that wrote it?

scenes.title: A Brilliant Student
narration: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891.
As a child he faced unfair treatment, but he never stopped studying.
He studied in India, the USA and England and became a great scholar.

scenes.title: Father of the Constitution
narration: He was the chairman of the committee that drafted India's Constitution.
He fought for equality, so that every person gets the same rights.
He was given the Bharat Ratna in 1990.

scenes.title: Remembering Babasaheb
narration: We celebrate Ambedkar Jayanti on 14 April.
He taught us: educate, agitate and organise.
Think about it: how can you treat everyone in your class equally?
